summary: Working in Buddhist studies and other fields, Lorne Ladner studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (attested 2004). He served as an adjunct faculty member in the counseling program at Argosy University (attested 2004).

Lothar Ledderose is a scholar of sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Princeton University (~1969–1970) and Harvard University (~1970–1972), later holding posts at Heidelberg University as Professor (~1976–2009) and the University of Cambridge (~1992–1993).

Specializing in sinology and history/archaeology, Lothar von Falkenhausen held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993) and served as a visiting professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in 2003.

Louis Dumont was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Collège d'Harcourt, EHESS, EPHE, and Institut d'ethnologie under Marcel Mauss (~1936–1939). He held positions at ATP (1937–1951), Oxford (1951–1955), EPHE (1955), and EHESS (attested 1985).

Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology after studying at the École des chartes (1884–1888). He was the first director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1898–1904) and later held posts at the Collège de France (1920–1935).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1977–2007).

Specializing in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, Louis H. Gray studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900). He held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1920–1921).

Louis Havet worked in linguistics and other fields, studying at EPHE under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne (~1868–1874). He was later appointed to a post at the Collège de France, serving from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Komjathy specializes in religious studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Boston University (~2000–2005) under Paul Rouzer and served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego (~2008).
Louis Ligeti was an Iranian/Central Asian, sinology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1921–1925) and the University of Paris under Paul Pelliot (1925–1928).

Louis Renou was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, and under Antoine Meillet at ENLOV. He served as Director at the University of Paris (~1937–1966) and Membre de l'Institut (~1946–1966).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Charles de Harlez, Philippe Colinet, Victor Henry, Sylvain Lévi, and Hendrik Kern, later holding professorships at Ghent University (1894–1929) and Free University of Brussels (~1921–1938).

A scholar of sinology, linguistics, and Indology, Louis-Mathieu Langlès studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as Chief Keeper of Manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and as Administrateur and Persian chair holder at INALCO (~1795–1824).

Louise Child works in religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under Sibnath Sarma, also studying under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Luboš Bělka specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and later held a post there (~1989).

Specializing in history/archaeology and Indology, Luca Maria Olivieri earned his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin (~2005–2010). He served as director at IsMEO (~2011) and became Associate Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~2021).

Lucia Dolce works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She has held posts at SOAS University of London, including Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and Associate Professor (attested 2015).
Lucia Galli is a scholar in Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.
Lucian Scherman was a scholar of Indology and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1881–1885) and subsequently held a post there (~1893–1936).
